closedFirstPassFindings: Working state now lives inside the conversation or context/evidence surface instead of depending on a floating global proof strip.
Project context visibly resolves into the right inspector and becomes stable product context.
Evidence registers into provenance only when evidence-source-added fixture events arrive.
Structured Recommendation resolves by completed section rather than animating a fully visible finished answer.
Approval begins in neutral advisory presentation and crosses into consequence language only when approval-required arrives.
Execution uses present-tense language only for the active operation and completed-language labels for settled work.
Execution completion resolves into a restrained Decision → Action → Verified → History lineage rather than celebration.
Mobile now demonstrates the actual project/thread continuity sheet instead of only animating its trigger.
qualitativeStrengths: Motion is much more product-native and less like an observability/proof overlay.
The six-moment sequence tells AI Council's product story without introducing a separate motion aesthetic.
Counterpoint remains the reading/conversation rhythm, Decision Spine owns provenance and settlement, and Threshold remains rare and consequential.
The strongest motion remains the advice → approval boundary, which is appropriate because authority genuinely changes there.
The execution sequence communicates progress without fake percentage completion or spectacle.
remainingProductionRisks: Production runtime adapters still need to emit the event vocabulary; current browser telemetry is explicitly fixture evidence.
The Structured Recommendation proof should eventually cover a real multi-section production response with variable section lengths and asynchronous readiness.
Evidence acquisition needs production tests with large source counts and sources arriving out of order.
The mobile sheet needs focus trapping, escape/back behavior, touch target and reduced-motion accessibility proof in the implemented product.
Execution progress needs cancellation, partial failure, rollback and retry paths before final Visual System approval.
